finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::new unauthenticated webhook endpoint is exempted from rate limiting (`@skipthrottle`) while the body is fully parsed (up to 25mb) and the raw bytes retained *before* the hmac guard runs — unauthenticated dos amplification
evidence: The code facts are as described: yorkie-event.controller.ts:31-34 puts `@SkipThrottle()` and only `YorkieSignatureGuard` (no JWT) on `POST /internal/yorkie/events`, app.module.ts registers `ThrottlerGuard` as the sole global `APP_GUARD` (120/60s), and main.ts:45-56 parses every JSON body at the 25MB `JSON_BODY_LIMIT` and retains the full raw Buffer specifically for this path — all as Express middleware, i.e. before Nest guards, so an unauthenticated caller reaches parse + raw-buffer retention + a 25MB HMAC (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:52-54) before the 401, at an unbounded rate. Nothing in the repo restricts `/internal/*`; the "internal cluster URL, no public exposure" is only an ops note in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md. The claim overstates the delta slightly: because `ThrottlerGuard` is itself a Nest guard, the 25MB parse also happens before the 429 on every other route, so `@SkipThrottle` removes the sustained-request cap rather than enabling the parse cost per se — which is why I rate this a real but modest hardening gap rather than a serious DoS hole.
